newsitem.title: USA: TRW to buy Magna units for $418 million.
newsitem.headline: TRW to buy Magna units for $418 million.

text.p: TRW Inc. said Monday it will acquire two European units of Magna International Inc. for $418 million as part of an alliance of the two companies to produce automotive products for the global market.
The companies said TRW will lead development efforts in air bags, seat belts, inflators, sensors and steering wheels, while Magna will focus on vehicle interiors and body systems.

As part of the deal, TRW will buy an 80 percent equity interest in two Magna-owned German units -- MST Automotive GmbH Automobil-Sicherheitstechnik and Temic Bayern-Chemie Airbag GmbH -- for $418 million in cash.
MST is a European supplier of air bag modules, steering wheels and other related automotive components. Temic makes air bag inflators and propellants and related automotive components.
Magna, based in Markham, Ontario, is a $5 billion automotive supplier with more than 35,000 employees in 120 manufacturing operations and other facilities in 11 countries.

Cleveland-based TRW provides advanced technology products and services for the automotive, space and defence, and systems integration markets. It employs approximately 63,000 people in 27 countries, and is one of the largest independent automotive components suppliers in the world.
Magna's stock gained 62.5 cents to $55.375 while TRW slipped 62.5 cents to $47, both in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
